policy: Run after routing review. These cases intentionally pin the specialist architecture so they test whether the agent can execute a selected tool correctly, not whether it can route to that tool.

priority_cases.implementation_prompt:
Implement the requested experience system in this repository.

Use the project's existing Anime.js v4.5.0 motion system. Do not add GSAP, Motion, Three.js/R3F, or another animation engine.

Requirements:
- On larger screens, the experience/project items should form a loose orbiting/living composition around a central project object.
- Items must be draggable with appropriate release/snap behavior.
- Switching between Experience and Projects must smoothly reorganize the same semantic DOM elements into a clean structured layout/state.
- Design a touch/mobile interaction that is appropriate for small screens rather than forcing the desktop orbit onto mobile.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion while preserving all content and controls.
- Use version-correct Anime.js v4 APIs from the installed package; inspect package/types/docs if uncertain.
- Integrate cleanly with React lifecycle and remove/revert animation state on unmount.
- Preserve the fixture's visual language rather than redesigning the whole site.

Run the build and report what you changed, including any lifecycle, mobile, and reduced-motion decisions.

Implement the project-media effect in this repository using curtainsjs@8.1.6 as the bounded DOM+GPU layer. Install exactly curtainsjs@8.1.6 if it is not already present.

Requirements:
- Preserve the existing project grid as semantic DOM: links, headings, descriptions, layout, and SEO content must remain normal HTML.
- Apply WebGL only to the project media surfaces.
- Add a refined liquid/refraction distortion that responds to pointer movement on capable desktop devices.
- Add a more dramatic shader-driven visual transition when a project link is activated, without rebuilding routing or the whole page in WebGL.
- Do not introduce Three.js/R3F.
- Provide sensible touch/mobile behavior and a reduced-motion/non-WebGL fallback.
- Handle resize/scroll synchronization, WebGL context/resource cleanup, and unmounting correctly.
- Keep GPU work bounded to this section and avoid an unnecessary always-on render loop when the effect is inactive/offscreen.
- Keep the visual treatment coherent with the existing restrained fixture.

Run the build and report the implementation, fallback behavior, and cleanup/performance decisions.
priority_cases.defer_reason: The pinned curtainsjs@8.1.6 case is a valid legacy WebGL compatibility test, but the same author now actively publishes gpu-curtains as a WebGPU rewrite/successor. Do not silently replace the pin. Decide whether Layer C should test legacy WebGL compatibility, modern WebGPU, or both before running I4.

priority_cases.implementation_prompt:
Implement the bounded experience-constellation visualization in this repository using pixi.js@8.19.0. Install exactly pixi.js@8.19.0 if it is not already present.

Requirements:
- Render roughly 500 interactive logo/image nodes in one bounded visualization section.
- Nodes should drift subtly, respond to pointer proximity, support selection/filtering, and smoothly regroup by category.
- Use PixiJS v8 patterns appropriate to the installed version.
- Keep the surrounding page in normal React/Next.js DOM; do not migrate the site into canvas or 3D.
- Do not use Three.js/R3F.
- Avoid 500 continuously animated React DOM nodes.
- Implement sensible batching/render-loop ownership and pause or reduce work when the visualization is offscreen.
- Design a lower-cost mobile/touch mode.
- Provide an accessible semantic representation/control surface for the same meaningful items outside or alongside the canvas.
- Clean up the Pixi application, listeners, textures/resources, and observers on unmount.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion without removing access to the content.

Run the build and report the rendering, performance, accessibility, and cleanup decisions.
